title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
supports: A lifecycle structure for governing, mapping, measuring, and managing AI risk and trustworthiness characteristics.
limitation: Use of the voluntary framework does not establish legal compliance, product quality, or fitness for a particular hiring process.

title: AI Risk Management Framework Playbook
supports: Suggested actions for applying the AI RMF functions across design, deployment, evaluation, and operation.
limitation: The suggested actions are optional and use-case agnostic; they are not a certification checklist or employment-law opinion.

title: Employment Tests and Selection Procedures
supports: Technical assistance on job-related selection procedures, discriminatory impact, validation, and employer responsibility.
limitation: The page describes federal considerations but does not determine whether a specific tool, employer, or use is lawful.

title: 29 CFR Part 1607: Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures
supports: The federal text governing documentation, impact, and validity evidence for covered employee selection procedures.
limitation: Reading the regulation does not resolve coverage, statistical sufficiency, defenses, or obligations in a particular matter.

title: Algorithms, Artificial Intelligence, and Disability Discrimination in Hiring
jurisdiction: United States disability and employment context
supports: Guidance on disability-related screening risk, accommodations, accessibility, notice, and measuring job skills rather than disability.
limitation: The informal guidance is not a final agency action and cannot decide whether a particular process complies with the ADA.

title: Job Analysis
supports: A practical account of job analysis as the foundation for defining tasks, competencies, and assessment content.
limitation: Federal personnel practice does not by itself validate a private-sector role brief or every automated assessment.

title: Structured Interviews
supports: Guidance on using predetermined job-related questions, consistent administration, and common rating standards.
limitation: Structure improves comparability but does not guarantee validity, fairness, accessibility, or a correct hiring decision.

organization: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
title: Responsible AI in Recruitment
supports: Procurement and deployment questions covering purpose, governance, accessibility, assurance, testing, pilots, transparency, and monitoring.
limitation: The guide expressly does not provide legal assurance and its examples are not universal deployment instructions.

title: AI Tools Used in Recruitment: Audit Outcomes
supports: Observed privacy and information-rights issues in recruitment sourcing, screening, and selection tools, plus remediation themes.
limitation: Consensual audits of selected providers do not establish prevalence, legal status, or performance of another product.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
supports: Testable web-content accessibility criteria across perceivability, operability, understandability, and robustness.
limitation: WCAG conformance covers web content and does not by itself prove that an end-to-end hiring process is accessible or lawful.

organization: New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
title: Automated Employment Decision Tools
supports: Official access to Local Law 144 materials on covered AEDT use, bias audits, public summaries, and candidate or employee notices.
limitation: The overview does not determine whether a system or use falls within the law's definitions or satisfies its requirements.

title: Navigating the AI Act
supports: Current Commission explanations of scope, risk classification, employment use cases, obligations, and implementation timing.
limitation: The FAQ is explanatory, timing can change, and classification depends on intended purpose and the facts of a deployment.

title: Mira: The First End-to-End AI Recruiter
supports: A first-party description of a recruiting-native multi-agent architecture and its handoffs.
limitation: It does not independently validate product performance, customer outcomes, legal compliance, or suitability for another workflow.

title: Agent Evaluation, Done Right
supports: A first-party evaluation model separating component, trajectory, and outcome evidence in agent systems.
limitation: The framework is not independent assurance and reported methods require reproduction in the buyer's own environment.

title: Performance Drift in Agent Systems
supports: A first-party account of why production agent behavior needs longitudinal evaluation and change-aware monitoring.
limitation: It does not prove the presence, absence, or rate of drift in a specific product or customer deployment.

title: Mira-Embeddings-V1: Domain-Adapted Semantic Reranking for Recruitment
supports: Reported retrieval and reranking metrics, dataset protocols, and boundary-aware modeling in a recruitment use case.
limitation: Reported metrics are dataset- and protocol-specific and do not establish live-role quality, fairness, or general superiority.

title: When AI Meets Recruiting: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
supports: A lifecycle taxonomy of AI applications and open questions across recruiting stages.
limitation: A review and taxonomy do not validate a product, an employer decision, or a universal division of human and machine work.

title: Hiring Outcomes, Not More Software
supports: A first-party argument for evaluating recruiting systems by delivered hiring progress and operating burden.
limitation: The product perspective is not an independent ROI study or evidence that the stated delivery model fits every employer.
